description: Source-lore pass 18 imports fleet organization and ship-to-ship combat while linking repeated tracking material to the canonical tracking entry.

entries.title: Fleet Control
entries.summary: Fleet command coordinates formation, routes, supplies, maintenance, discipline, communication, scouting, readiness, reinforcement, repairs, cargo, weather, and evacuation across multiple vessels.
body: A fleet is an organization in motion. Its commander must keep ships in formation, coordinate routes and communication, distribute [[water-in-the-skies|water]], food, ammunition, fuel, and crews, and ensure that damaged or undermanned vessels do not break the mission apart.

Fleet discipline and morale matter as much as navigation. Theft, inter-crew fights, conflicting captains, poor orders, and unequal supply can create rebellion or leave ships behind. Reinforcements and crew reallocation must reach the vessels that need them before shortages become disasters.

Scouts and weather watchers identify threats and dangerous skies. Engineers schedule docking and repairs. Cargo officers prioritize critical stores. Combat officers form defensive screens, prepare weapons, and execute maneuvers under pressure.

Failure cascades. A missed storm damages ships; damaged ships slow formation; delays consume supplies; shortages reduce morale; low morale breaks discipline and command. Effective fleet leadership therefore combines tactical, logistical, technical, and interpersonal authority.

sections.heading: Legacy Fleet Challenges
body: The source provides nineteen fleet-management checks with DCs and outcomes for coordination, navigation, supply, maintenance, discipline, morale, readiness, communication, reinforcement, scouting, formation, evacuation, crew allocation, tactics, repairs, cargo, and weather. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Ship-to-Ship Combat
entries.summary: Airship battles proceed through movement, action, and reaction phases involving positioning, mounted weapons, repairs, morale, concealment, boarding, evasive maneuvers, and evacuation.
body: Ship combat uses movement, action, and reaction phases. Every vessel moves according to speed and piloting decisions, then fires weapons or performs specialized work, and may react defensively to enemy action.

Wind, turbulence, propulsion, and magical influence alter movement. Sail-powered craft gain or lose speed with wind direction; storms reduce control; etheric or magical systems may remain more consistent.

During the action phase, crews fire [[ship-based-weapons|mounted weapons]], repair systems, rally troops, erect barricades, teleport, cloak the vessel, deploy smoke, or launch boarding parties. Personal attacks can target exposed crew, but ordinary handheld weapons and common spells cannot meaningfully damage protected hulls.

Reactions include evasive maneuvers, bracing for impact, deploying shields or counter-projectiles, and emergency evacuation. Victory depends on crew availability, firing arcs, ammunition, positioning, damage control, morale, and whether a captain seeks destruction, capture, escape, or boarding.
Open-sky detection and pursuit use the canonical [[ship-tracking|ship-tracking system]].

sections.heading: Legacy Combat Procedure
body: The source provides grid movement, attack and critical-hit rules, repair values, morale bonuses, defensive modifiers, countermeasure percentages, evacuation capacity, and a repeated tracking and detection table. Numerical rules require conversion; repeated tracking is indexed through `ship-tracking`.
